thread:
anna: Heads-up — telemetry spike showing a lot of requests being routed to the fallback capacity when requests originate from projectless service-account keys. Quota billing is attributing to org-default instead of the customer project, which skews our per-project metering. Anyone seen this pattern before?

mike: Noted. Can you paste the minimal repro logs? curious if it's a header parity thing or our router fallback criteria.

anna: Paste from the gateway logs (sanitized):
```
SRC=X-Forwarded-For: 34.23.1.2
AUTH=Bearer <service-key>
ORIGIN_HEADER=org: none; project: none
ROUTER_DECISION=fallback-spot
QUOTA_ID=org-default
```
We expect `ORIGIN_HEADER` to contain a project id for SA tokens but a previous change to the exchange path returns empty for projectless tokens and router falls back to cheaper pool.

sasha: That matches my earlier notes about exchange v2. When the token has only a service-account id and no explicit project claim, our router treats it as tenantless. Quick win: make router prefer origin-derived attribution from service-account->project mapping before falling back. But we need to consider performance of the map lookup.

jia: If we change routing to consult SA->project mapping synchronously we'll add latency on the hot path. Alternative: do an async enrichment step and route based on a cached effective-tenant table with TTL. Telemetry should tell us cache hit ratio.

mike: I like the cached-lookup approach. We can add a fast-path: if SA token includes `project` claim do nothing, else consult cache, else fallback. Cache misses increment a telemetry counter so we can monitor.

product-ops: UX ask — the Console should surface "effective tenant" for every request when available, and show whether it was derived from claim vs cached lookup vs fallback. That will help customers and support see why billing shows org-default.

sasha: Agreed. Also add a flag in rollout to keep old behavior until we verify sampling is clean. We should expose a `routing.attribution_mode` remote config with values `legacy|cache-lookup|strict-claim`.

anna: Implementation plan suggestion: 1) Add cache-lookup in router (TTL 5m) + telemetry counters (cache_hit, cache_miss, stale_lookup), 2) Console change to display effective_tenant + derivation reason, 3) Start a 10% canary with `cache-lookup` then ramp. Rollback on increase in p50 latency > 10ms or jump in quota misattribution.

jia: I'll own the telemetry counters and tracing spans. I'll add counters under `router.attribution.*` and a sampling trace for cache misses. Also will add a gate in datadog dashboard for the canary.

mike: I'll implement the cache and the `routing.attribution_mode` flag. Will try to keep lookup O(1) and sharded to avoid lock contention.

product-ops: Timeline request — can we aim for a canary by EOD Friday? If not, what's the earliest? We need the Console changes to land before ramp so support can interpret metrics.

anna: EOD Friday is tight. Proposal: small canary with telemetry-only change tomorrow (no routing switch) to capture current miss rate + sample traces. Console mockups by Wednesday. Full cache-lookup canary next week.

deploybot: deploybot: created rollout ticket #ROLL-9123 (canary/attribution-cache) — linked to PRs.

anna: Sounds good. For compliance/privacy: Sasha, can you confirm the cache doesn't increase exposure of PII and that we hash keys before storing?

sasha: Will enforce one-way hash + salt per-region. Also ensure KMS for salt rotation. I'll add a small doc snippet.

anna: Great — thanks everyone. Jia, Mike, please sync in 15 and we'll lock the canary gating thresholds.

mike: On it.

jia: On it.

anna: :thumbsup:
